questions.answer: Noticing, interpreting and appropriately responding to signals.
questions.feedback: Do not equate it with perfection.

questions.prompt: What does a pooled positive correlation indicate?
questions.answer: An average positive association under the studied measures and samples.
questions.feedback: It is not an individual prediction.

questions.prompt: Does r=0.25 mean 25% of children are secure because of sensitivity?
questions.answer: No; correlation is not a causal proportion or percentage of people.
Current environments and resources can influence behaviour independently of early experiences.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only.
scoring.practice: Explains developmental influences and interprets group-level evidence without deterministic causation or caregiver blame.
scoring.transfer: Construct a fictional three-stage developmental map with resources at two levels and competing explanations. Critique a deterministic early-experience claim and identify a feasible current support, including its limits.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; no averaging away omissions or safety-critical criteria. No automatic competency award.
